parsed.explanation: The combined regime imposes universal-exposure measures on every trans visitor: national passports and visas are issued only per birth sex, an X marker is unavailable, entry officers are instructed to refuse and even permanently bar applicants suspected of sex 'misrepresentation', and reported confiscations have stranded travellers. Federal custody and immigration detention show documented severe harm (forced labour, sexual abuse, denial of hormones). The division adds a binding birth-sex facility rule for state buildings, closed birth-certificate recognition, no gender-identity discrimination or hate-crime protection, and a documented arrest of a trans woman under its facility law with a men's-ward holding. State threat-framing is explicit at both levels. Mitigation is partial and contested: hate-crime and employment backstops, some courts enjoining orders, marriage recognition, and patchy municipal protections. This is unremedied tier-1/2 exposure with incomplete, unevenly working recourse — solidly Elevated Risk, low in band.

entry_documents.exposure: Passports/visas issued only per birth sex; X markers stopped; officers instructed to refuse cases with document/sex doubt and consider lifetime fraud ineligibility; travellers report confiscation and stranding; foreign governments issued advisories after detentions.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid until expiry; policy under active court challenge; limited waiver for fraud findings.
entry_documents.interaction: Document doubt at entry can escalate to refusal, fraud allegation, detention and birth-sex custody.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National corrections policies mandate hormone removal and forced 'therapy'; immigration custody shows forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse of trans men; reporting on trans prisoners stopped. Division's facility law debates contemplate solitary confinement for incarcerated trans people.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Some executive orders enjoined; rescinded prison protections not restored.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Any entry refusal or arrest routes into these custody regimes.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Facility bans by birth sex in government buildings across ~19 state/provinces, some criminalised; the division bans identity-congruent facilities in public schools and state buildings, with a documented trespass arrest of a trans woman and 24-hour men's-ward holding.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Most states have no mapped ban; the trespass offence requires willful entry plus refusal to depart, not automatic arrest; exemptions exist.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal order bars identity-congruent use in federally funded single-sex facilities; state rules compound it.

care_services.exposure: Hospital-records subpoenas, frozen youth services, proposed public-insurance exclusion; division bans under-18 care with mandated wind-down; 2022 contract termination shows state hostility to trans health provision.
care_services.protection: Settlement secured apology, $300,000 and non-discrimination commitment; adult care for visitors not banned.
care_services.interaction: Travelling minor's care access is blocked in-division; a parent faces the care ban and investigation climate.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: 'Gender ideology' framing across executive orders; teachers face prosecution for facilitating a minor's transition; counterterrorism strategy prioritises 'radically pro-transgender' groups; division allows business service denial on religious grounds.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National hate-crime statute and 2020 employment ruling backstops; some courts blocked orders.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Threat framing feeds the entry fraud lever and facility enforcement; courts partially counteract.

minors_guardians.exposure: Under-18 care banned in the division and 27 state/provinces; schools investigated; a trans student arrested under facility law; teachers criminalised for name/pronoun support.
minors_guardians.protection: Marriage and some municipal protections irrelevant to this; litigation ongoing.
minors_guardians.interaction: Travelling with a trans minor multiplies exposure via schools, care and facility rules.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Documented arrest under facility law with handcuffing and men's-ward holding; hate-crime coverage absent in-division; 190+ anti-trans bills in 2023 signal normalised hostility.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute; 22+ state/provinces with anti-discrimination law; other states' police prosecute bias attacks.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police response varies sharply by state/province; visitor cannot choose protections in-division.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Complaints routinely fail where bans operate; oversight findings (birth-certificate ruling) confirm exclusion rather than relief; custody oversight reporting curtailed.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Some injunctions, the passport suit, municipal ordinances and a national FAQ partially operate; enforcement of protections documented in other states.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedy depends on forum and timing; many measures in litigation, so operative exposure shifts with court rulings.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.35-A has one unremedied birth-sex facility rule with court-confirmed exclusion. This jurisdiction has the same tier-1 facility exposure in-division plus a broader federal document/entry regime with a fraud bar, documented custody abuse, and official threat framing — worse than 0.35-A.

0.45-D's repeated unremedied invasive screening parallels the passport/entry exposure here, but this regime adds criminalised facility bans with arrests, custody harm, and care bans for minors — materially below 0.45-D.

0.55-A lacks any universal-exposure rule; exposures are commercial refusals with partial remedy. This jurisdiction's unremedied universal facility, document and entry measures keep it well below 0.55-A, though its working courts and backstop statutes stop it falling to 0.25.

parsed.synthesis: The combined operative regime starts from a hostile federal layer — birth-sex passports, an entry fraud lever, federally funded facility exclusion, and documented custody harm — that every trans visitor passes through, then compounds it with an in-division facility ban, closed birth-certificate recognition, no local gender-identity protections, and a care ban for minors. A traveller with any document discrepancy can move from entry questioning to refusal, fraud finding or birth-sex custody, and custody outcomes are documented as abusive. Counterweights exist — national hate-crime and employment backstops, enjoined orders, active litigation, marriage recognition and patchy municipal protections — but the record shows them failing to displace the operative exposures (the arrest occurred under the facility law; the birth-certificate ruling excluded rather than relieved). The regime resembles 0.35-A/0.45-A in kind but broader in scope, sitting at the top of Elevated Risk.
